newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks follow Wall St down at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks follow Wall St down at open.

text.p: Australian shares opened down sharply on Friday after the Dow dropped nearly 50 points on Thursday with U.S. investors putting the breaks on the Wall Street market ahead of the release of a crucial payroll and wage report later today.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index slipped 18 points to 2,239.4 while September share price index futures dived 22 points to 2,230, a 9.4 points discount to the underlying index.
Brokers said the market was reacting predictably to Wall Street's move, with blue chip issues opening down in unison.

"The market is putting up a fight at current levels. It held well against a weak futures market yesterday so I'm predicting it won't fall much further than 20 points today," a Perth-based dealer said.

The dealer said he expected the industrial sector to fair best against the poorer sentiment created by nervous U.S. markets, particularly those companies that have recently announced better than expected earnings.
"The big transport groups like TNT and Brambles should hold reasonably well and Amcor could see some bargain hunting," the dealer said.
The outlook for the resources sector was less optimistic with dealers saying weaker base metal prices would keep the share prices of the major miners in the red.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to three, while about 38 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
